status: Proposed exact typed native FS read/reset additions; source-only independent event/ownership review requested before production mutation.

h_edits.after:
/* Reset the same native request after its actual completion was removed from
 * the FIFO and request_cleanup ran. A new/unsubmitted request also admits its
 * initial Reset. In-flight, still-queued or uncleaned operations return
 * UV_EBUSY without changing state. No wrapper, event, backing or request is
 * allocated by Reset.
 *
 * The previous dequeued event entitlement may remain owned while the request
 * is submitted again, as in FileHandleReadWrap's original completion callback.
 * After Reset the old event may ONLY be released: its mutable completion info
 * now belongs to the next operation. Stable event release fields never change,
 * and its next link must not be touched by the old owner. Each actual queued
 * completion still transfers one independent request and service entitlement.
 */
int pi_uv_fs_request_reset(PiUvFsRequest *request);
/* Native FileHandle/StreamResource span: the caller supplies the exact
 * uv_buf_t base/length and keeps its native storage owner alive through actual
 * completion and request_cleanup. This call borrows bytes and makes no JS
 * wrapper/lease, copy or extra native allocation. The library does not infer
 * or extend that external buffer lifetime. Wrong state/invalid native span
 * returns UV_EINVAL before admission. Windows requires its real ULONG extent.
 */
int pi_uv_fs_read_buffer(PiUvFsRequest *request, int descriptor,
    char *base, size_t length, int64_t position);
int pi_uv_fs_read(PiUvFsRequest *request, int descriptor,

protocol: One existing PiUvFsRequest remains the actual uv_fs_t storage and has one embedded event slot. There is no per-dispatch allocation, second loop/service, raw loop export, JS value, or callback execution on the worker.

The worker unlinks the completed native request and decrements actual pending_requests, then publishes event_queued before completed. An acquire observation of completed cannot see the pre-queued window. The worker then owns its queued-event entitlement before existing FIFO publication.
The existing FIFO next operation removes the slot and clears event_queued under its mutex before handing the event to the host. Reset requires actual completed+cleaned and not queued.

An old event entitlement may survive Reset and resubmission, but its mutable info is no longer inspectable. Only event_release remains valid. That routine reads stable service, source, keeper, accepted, storage and allocation fields; the FS branch only drops one independent request and service entitlement and never changes event.next.

A new actual completion can therefore enqueue that same embedded slot before the prior host event is retired. It owns another request/service entitlement, and old event_release cannot unlink the new queue entry.

Reset changes only port admission/bookkeeping and req.data at the original ReqWrap Reset boundary; it never pretends cleanup or event dequeue happened. Old callbacks may finish their final atomic request release after reuse; their request owner remains independently alive.
FileHandle's actual EmitAlloc storage owner, normally the Environment managed-buffer map, is the borrowed native span lifetime authority. The raw API does not obtain a JS lease or an earlier wrapper.
The existing lease-based read, admission/cancel/completion/cleanup algorithms, TCP endpoint behavior and original FS14/TCP12 controls remain unchanged except additive FS dequeue bookkeeping.

The initial proposed queued/completed publication order was corrected before production mutation. Accepted operations cannot pass Reset between completed publication and queue insertion; event_queued is already true. Immediate native admission rejection has no event and remains distinguishable by accepted=false.
planned_controls: Real raw buffer reads and offsets with no JS backing object; caller storage remains alive through stop/join.

Cleaned and dequeued first completion is reset and resubmitted while the first event entitlement remains owned; second completion queues before first event release; exact bytes, request identity and reference/queue accounting.
FIFO order with another real request while one embedded event slot is reused, proving old release does not clear the newly published next link.
Reject reset while in-flight/still queued or before cleanup without changing the request; initial no-op Reset uses the same storage.
Mix real JS-lease read and native span reuse so cleanup/Reset releases prior backing exactly once.
Shutdown/cancellation with a reused actual request preserves one callback per accepted dispatch and joins before native buffer retirement.
open_scope: The actual FileHandleReadWrap/template/freelist constructor and single FS Controller callback routing are next native consumers, not supplied by this raw bridge.
Original ReadStart ignores its Dispatch return; this API does not synthesize an immediate callback for it.
Full native trace and backing retry policy remain separate required StreamBase inputs.
The new FS request bookkeeping adds one atomic native field; no native allocation-size parity beyond actual charged storage is claimed.
